chunks.arabic_text: وَ سُئِلَ مُوسَى بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَمُوتُ أَ يُكَفَّنُ فِي ثَلَاثَةِ أَثْوَابٍ بِغَيْرِ قَمِيصٍ

translations.en: Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام was asked about a man who dies: may he be shrouded in three garments without a shirt?

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ «لَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ وَ الْقَمِيصُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ.»

translations.en: He said: “There is no problem with that, and the shirt is more preferred to me.”

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the shrouding of the deceased. It states that shrouding a dead person in three garments without a shirt is permissible, though including a shirt is preferred.
en.seo_question: Can a deceased person be shrouded in three garments without a qamīs?

key_terms.قَمِيصٍ: a shirt used as part of the shroud
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection or problem
